title: Travelers Want 'Plot Twist Trips' to Show Their Wild Side
paragraphs: For many people, holidays tend to follow a familiar pattern, whether it is a beach resort, a city break or a return visit to a favorite destination. However, according to the travel company Booking.com, a growing number of travelers now want their trips to reveal a completely different side of themselves.

In October 2026, Booking.com published its travel predictions for 2027, based on research involving more than 28,000 travelers around the world. One of the nine trends it identified is what it calls "plot twist trips." In a story, a plot twist is a sudden and unexpected change in events. Similarly, these are holidays that are chosen specifically because they surprise other people, or even the travelers themselves.

According to the research, 77% of travelers are interested in choosing a holiday specifically to do something "completely out of character." Furthermore, 36% want to surprise their friends and family with their holiday choices, and Booking.com suggests that other people's reactions are part of the attraction. As the company put it, "The best souvenir? The look on everyone else's face."
Social media also appears to play a role. Nearly three in 10 travelers, or 29%, said they had deleted or avoided posting about a holiday because it seemed too predictable or ordinary.

The report also identified several other trends. For example, 65% of travelers said they were interested in paranormal experiences, such as visiting places associated with ghosts. In addition, 81% said they would choose a destination mainly because of how it makes them feel, rather than where it is, and 64% said they would like AI to cover their work while they are away on holiday.
Booking.com also named several destinations that it expects to become popular in 2027, including Reims in France, Monterey in California and Sendai in Japan.
It should be noted, however, that these findings come from a travel company's own research, and the full details of the survey have not been published.
